mainTopic: Who can pledge and be the subject of ערכין and נדרים, and what the word הכל adds in our משנה and in the parallel משניות about סמיכה and תמורה by an heir.
overview: The משנה opens מסכת ערכין with a broad rule. Everyone can pledge ערכין and נדרים and can be the subject of them. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס cannot be valuated, because a ערך applies only to a definite male or a definite female. A חרש, שוטה and קטן cannot make pledges, because they lack דעת. The גמרא asks what each word adds. מעריכין adds a מופלא סמוך לאיש. נערכין adds a מנוול and a מוכה שחין, since the word נפשת shows that every living person has a ערך. נודרין is written only as a partner to נידרין, and נידרין adds a baby under a month old. The גמרא then asks the same question about הכל סומכין and הכל ממירין, and answers that both include an heir, against רבי יהודה. It brings the ברייתא where they argue and each side's source: רבי יהודה learns from קרבנו, and the רבנן learn from המר ימיר. It also explains how each side uses the three times קרבנו appears. The last answer for רבי יהודה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone can make and be the subject of valuations and vows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the general rule: everyone can make ערכין and נדרים and can be the subject of them. This includes כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, women and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone can pledge a valuation and can be valuated. Everyone can vow a person's worth and can be the subject of such a vow. This includes כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, women and slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכתא with a wide, inclusive rule about who takes part in ערכין and נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four roles here. מעריך is the one who pledges a valuation, and נערך is the one being valuated. נודר is the one who vows a person's market worth, and נידר is the one whose worth is vowed. ערכין uses a fixed amount from the Torah based on age and gender. A נדר uses what the person would sell for in the market as a slave. The list shows that all of these groups fit every role.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, the core text the גמרא will discuss
They pledge a valuation, saying 'the ערך of so-and-so is on me'
They are valuated; someone can pledge their fixed ערך
They vow to give a person's market value, saying 'his worth is on me'
They are the subject of such a vow; others can pledge their market worth

steps.whatToRemember: There are four roles: מעריך, נערך, נודר and נידר. ערך is a fixed amount from the Torah. A נדר is the person's actual market value.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערכין and נדרים. ערכין is a set amount from ויקרא 27 that depends only on age and gender. A נדר of a person's worth depends on what that specific person would sell for.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Everyone pledges valuations
phrases.notes: This means saying 'the ערך of so-and-so is on me,' which obligates paying the fixed amount from ויקרא 27.

phrases.english: and is valuated,
vows a person's worth and is the subject of such a vow
priests, Levites and Israelites,
women and slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה and the מסכתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All people, including כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, women and slaves, can make and be the subject of both ערכין and נדרים.

steps.title: A person of uncertain gender can vow but cannot be valuated
steps.stepSummary: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can make vows, be vowed about and make ערכין. They cannot be valuated, because only a definite male or a definite female has a ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can vow, can be vowed about, and can pledge valuations, but they cannot be valuated. Only someone who is definitely male or definitely female can be valuated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first exception to the general rule. A person whose gender is unclear cannot be the one being valuated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah sets different ערך amounts for males and females. So without a clear gender, there is no amount to apply. A נדר is based on market value, not gender, so they can still be vowed about. Making a pledge only needs a mature mind, so they can also pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose genitals are covered, so the gender is unknown
A person with both male and female features
A definite male
A definite female

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ערכין depends on clear gender categories, while נדרים do not. That difference comes up again and again in this מסכתא.

phrases.english: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
vow, are the subject of a vow, and pledge valuations,
but they are not valuated,
because no one is valuated except
a definite male and a definite female.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס נוֹדְרִין וְנִידָּרִין וּמַעֲרִיכִין אֲבָל לֹא נֶעֱרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First exception to the general rule of step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can take part in every role except being valuated, since ערך applies only to a definite male or female.

steps.title: Those without mature understanding can be valuated but cannot vow
steps.stepSummary: A חרש, שוטה and קטן can be vowed about and valuated. They cannot make vows or pledges themselves, because they lack דעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a child can be vowed about and valuated. They cannot vow or pledge a valuation themselves, because they lack mature understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second exception. These people can be the subject of a pledge, but they cannot make one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a vow is a legal commitment, and that requires דעת. Being the subject of a vow needs nothing from the person. Someone else is the one who pledges and pays. So these people are excluded only from the active roles.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, assumed to lack legal understanding
A mentally incompetent person
A minor, a child not yet of legal age
Mature understanding needed to make a legal commitment

steps.whatToRemember: The two exceptions work in opposite directions. A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס can pledge but cannot be valuated. A חרש, שוטה and קטן can be valuated but cannot pledge.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor
are the subject of a vow and are valuated,
but they neither vow nor pledge valuations,
because they lack understanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second exception to the general rule, the reverse of step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה and קטן can be valuated and vowed about, but cannot vow or pledge, because they lack דעת.

steps.title: What does the word 'everyone' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's word הכל (everyone) is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Everyone pledges valuations.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the משנה's opening word. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to list the groups it includes. So the word הכל seems extra. The גמרא assumes it must be there to include some case that is not stated openly.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion and analysis of the משנה
To include what? This asks what an extra word adds

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'Everyone pledges valuations':
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא analyzes the opening word of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case not openly stated in the משנה is included by the word הכל?

steps.title: It includes a sharp child close to adulthood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that הכל includes a מופלא סמוך לאיש: a child in the year before adulthood who understands vows, and who can therefore pledge a valuation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a sharp child who is close to adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The word הכל adds a child near בר מצוה age who understands what he is saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a קטן cannot pledge because he lacks דעת. A מופלא סמוך לאיש is an exception. He is still a minor, but he is mature enough that his vow counts. This does not cancel the rule about a קטן. It is a special case within it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharp minor close to adulthood, in the year before coming of age, who understands vows

steps.confusionAlert: This child is still a קטן, a minor. He is not an adult. He is a special exception whose vow counts because he shows understanding.

phrases.english: To include a discerning minor close to adulthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes a מופלא סמוך לאיש, a mature minor near adulthood, as one who can pledge ערכין.

steps.title: What does 'everyone is valuated' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's word נערכין (everyone can be valuated) is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said everyone 'is valuated.' Which extra kind of person is this meant to include?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did with מעריכין, the גמרא now asks what the word נערכין adds. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stressed 'הכל' (everyone), which suggests that some person we might have left out is included. The גמרא wants to know who that person is on the side of being valuated, not on the side of making the pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: Are valuated: someone else can pledge the fixed Torah value (ערך) of these people
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: "Are valuated": what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question pattern as Step 4, now applied to the next word of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person is newly included by the משנה's statement that everyone is valuated?

steps.title: It includes a disfigured person and one covered with boils
steps.stepSummary: The word נערכין includes a מנוול (a repulsive-looking person) and a מוכה שחין (a person afflicted with boils).
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a repulsive-looking person and a person covered with boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word comes to include people who are very unattractive or sick with boils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people would be worth nothing if sold as slaves on the market. So one might think nobody could pledge their value. The משנה tells us they still have a ערך.

keyTerms.meaning: A repulsive or disgusting-looking person
A person afflicted with boils (a skin disease)

phrases.english: To include a repulsive person and one afflicted with boils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נערכין includes a מנוול and a מוכה שחין.

steps.title: Why we needed a special source for them
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that only someone with a market value (דמים) can have a ערך. The word נפשת teaches that anyone with life has a ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: the פסוק says 'a vow ... by your valuation,' linking ערכין to vows. So anyone who has a market value can be valuated, and anyone without a market value cannot. That would leave out the מנוול and the מוכה שחין. So it teaches us 'persons,' meaning anyone at all who is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it was even needed to include these people. It shows the mistake we would have made, then the word in the פסוק that fixes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistake (הוה אמינא) comes from the פסוק putting 'נדר' next to 'בערכך.' That might suggest ערכין depends on a person having a sellable value. The answer comes from the same פסוק: the word נפשת shows that a ערך depends only on being a living person. It does not depend on market worth.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say: the mistaken first thought
Market value: a vow to give what a person would sell for
Fixed values set by the תורה according to age and gender
It teaches us (the real lesson)
Persons, souls: any living person
Whatever it is, any amount at all

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up דמים and ערכין. דמים is a person's market price, which changes from person to person. ערך is a fixed amount from the תורה that does not depend on looks or health at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Anyone who is a living person has a ערך, even if they would be worth nothing on the market. The source is the word נפשת.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
It is written "a vow by your valuation,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:2. The words 'vow' and 'valuation' sit side by side in that פסוק.

phrases.english: so whoever has a market value has a valuation,
and whoever has no market value has no valuation.
So it teaches us "persons,"
phrases.notes: This word comes from the same פסוק: 'נדר בערכך נפשת לה׳.'

phrases.english: meaning anyone at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the inclusion in Step 7 was needed, and gives its source in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the word נפשת, we would have tied ערכין to market value. נפשת shows that every living person has a ערך.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule of ערכין: the fixed value depends only on being a living person of a certain age and gender. It does not depend on the person's worth on the market.

steps.title: What does 'everyone vows' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's word נודרין (everyone can vow) is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said everyone 'vows.' Which extra kind of person is this meant to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next word of the משנה, נודרין, and asks what it adds. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מעריכין and נערכין, the גמרא found a person each word included. Now it asks the same about making a vow of someone's market value.

keyTerms.meaning: Make vows: here, vowing to give a person's market value to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: "Vow": what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question pattern again, now on the word נודרין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person is newly included by the משנה's statement that everyone vows?

steps.title: 'Vow' adds nothing; it is there for 'is vowed about'
steps.stepSummary: The word נודרין does not include anyone new. The משנה wrote it only because the next word, נידרין, was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was really 'is vowed about' that the משנה needed to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נודרין itself does not come to include anything. It was only written as a partner to נידרין, which did need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every word in a משנה must teach its own new case. Sometimes a word is there just to keep a pair together. Here the real point is in נידרין, and נודרין simply goes along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Are vowed about: someone else can vow to give their market value
It was needed (by the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not explain what נודרין includes. It says the word itself does not need its own lesson.

phrases.english: It needed to say "are vowed about."
phrases.notes: In other words, 'vow' was only written so that 'is vowed about' could be said right next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by saying the word does not need to include anything by itself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נודרין adds nothing on its own. It appears only because נידרין was needed.

steps.title: What does the word נידרין add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case is included by the משנה's word נידרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'נידרין' (everyone can be vowed about), what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained נערכין and נודרין, the גמרא now asks the same question about the next word, נידרין. This opens a search for what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נידרין means a person can be the subject of a vow of value, for example when someone says 'I pledge this person's market value.' The word הכל ('everyone') suggests it includes someone we might have left out, so the גמרא wants to know who.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be vowed about: someone can pledge this person's market value (דָּמִים) to the הֶקְדֵּשׁ
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: 'Are vowed about': what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 said נודרין was written because of נידרין, so the גמרא now asks what נידרין adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case is included by the word נידרין.

steps.title: Not טומטום, אנדרוגינוס, or חרש שוטה וקטן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects two possible answers, because those people are already named in our own משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes to include a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, the משנה teaches them openly! And if you say it comes to include a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן, the משנה teaches them openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests possible answers and knocks each one down. A word cannot be needed to include someone the משנה already names directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה itself says that טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, and also חרש שוטה וקטן, are נידרין. Since they are already written out, the general word נידרין is not needed for them.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose gender cannot be seen
A person with both male and female features
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
He teaches them openly, so there is no need to include them from an extra word

phrases.english: If it is to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
he teaches them explicitly!
phrases.notes: He means right here in our own משנה.

phrases.english: And if it is to include a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
he teaches them explicitly!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects possible answers to the question in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects טומטום/אנדרוגינוס and חרש שוטה וקטן as what נידרין comes to include.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: These cases are already stated openly in the משנה, so the extra word is not needed for them.

steps.title: Not a baby under a month, and not a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects two more possible answers, because those cases are taught openly in later משניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes to include a baby less than a month old, the משנה teaches it openly! And if you say it comes to include a נכרי, the משנה teaches it openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps searching and rejects two more candidates. These cases also already appear openly in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby under thirty days has no ערך at all, but it does have a market value, so it can be נידר. A later משנה in this פרק says this openly, and it also rules openly about a נכרי. So it seems every candidate is already covered, and the word נידרין looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby less than thirty days old, which has no fixed ערך in the תורה
A non-Jew

phrases.english: If it is to include one less than a month old,
he teaches them explicitly!
phrases.notes: Here he means a later משנה in this פרק, not our opening משנה.

phrases.english: And if it is to include a gentile,
he teaches them explicitly!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues rejecting candidates, now using cases taught in later משניות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects פחות מבן חודש and נכרי as what נידרין adds.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both are taught openly in later משניות, so it seems the word is not needed for them.

steps.title: It does include the baby under a month: stated generally, explained later
steps.stepSummary: נידרין does include a baby under a month old. The משנה gives the general rule first and spells out the details later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it comes to include a baby less than a month old, and the משנה teaches it in general and then goes back and explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It goes back to one of the rejected options and shows why it still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection was that a later משנה states the baby's law openly. The answer is that this is no problem: a משנה may hint at a rule in a general word first and give the details later. So the later משנה does not make נידרין extra; it explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really: the answer goes back to an option that was pushed away
He teaches it in general and then explains it in detail

steps.whatToRemember: נידרין includes a baby under thirty days. It has no ערך, but it can be vowed about by its value. The later משנה just spells this out.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rejection in step 13 was wrong about the facts. The later משנה really does state it openly. The answer only explains why that is not a problem.

phrases.english: Actually, it is to include one less than a month old,
and he teaches it and then explains it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לְאֵתוֹיֵי פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְתָנֵי וַהֲדַר מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the baby option rejected in step 13 and removes the objection.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נידרין includes a baby under a month old. The משנה teaches it generally and explains it later.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a later משנה states the baby's law openly, נידרין cannot be meant for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A משנה may give a general rule first and explain it in detail later, so the later משנה does not make the word extra.

steps.title: What does 'everyone places hands' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to a similar משנה about סמיכה and asks what its word הכל includes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone places hands' — what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another משנה that also starts with הכל and asks the same kind of question. This sets up a short answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סמיכה means pressing one's hands on the head of a קרבן before it is brought. The word הכל suggests someone we might have left out is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone does סמיכה on a קרבן
Pressing one's hands on the animal's head before it is offered

phrases.english: 'Everyone places hands': what does it come to include?
phrases.notes: This is the opening of a משנה in מנחות, not our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'what does הכל include' question on a parallel משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is included by הכל in 'everyone places hands'.

steps.title: An heir does סמיכה, unlike רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: הכל סומכין includes an heir, who does סמיכה on the קרבן he inherited. This goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include an heir, and the משנה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the extra case is an heir who inherited a קרבן from his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think only the owner who set aside the קרבן does סמיכה. The word הכל teaches that even an heir does. רבי יהודה holds an heir does not, so this משנה follows the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: An heir, here someone who inherited a קרבן his father set aside
And this is not like the view of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: To include an heir,
and not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes an heir, against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: What does 'everyone substitutes' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the משנה in תמורה, 'everyone substitutes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone substitutes' — what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to one more משנה starting with הכל and asks what it includes. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה means trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one. The holy one stays holy, and the new animal also becomes holy. The question is who besides the original owner can do this.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone can make a תמורה
Swapping a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too

phrases.english: 'Everyone substitutes': what does it come to include?
phrases.notes: This is the opening of the משנה in מסכת תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 15, now applied to תמורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is included by הכל in 'everyone substitutes'.

steps.title: An heir can make a תמורה, unlike רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: הכל ממירין includes an heir, who can make a תמורה with the animal he inherited. This also goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include an heir, and the משנה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as for סמיכה: the extra case is an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an heir swaps a regular animal for his father's holy animal, the swap takes effect and the new animal becomes holy. רבי יהודה disagrees, so this משנה again follows the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: Something made holy and given to the Temple
Regular, non-holy animals or items

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'everyone places hands' and 'everyone substitutes' use הכל to include an heir. Both go against רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: To include an heir,
and not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with the same answer given in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes an heir making a תמורה, against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The ברייתא where the רבנן and רבי יהודה argue about an heir
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the first opinion lets an heir do סמיכה and תמורה, and רבי יהודה says he can do neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: an heir does סמיכה, and an heir can make a תמורה. רבי יהודה says: an heir does not do סמיכה, and an heir cannot make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up what it just said in steps 16 and 18: those readings of הכל go against רבי יהודה. It brings the ברייתא where רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16 and 18 said that הכל includes an heir, and that this goes against רבי יהודה. This ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה really holds this view, on both סמיכה and תמורה. So the two משניות in מנחות and תמורה follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An heir, here a son who inherited his father's קרבן
Leans his hands on the animal before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)
Makes a תמורה, trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one, which makes both animals holy

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: An heir places hands,
an heir can effect substitution.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
An heir does not place hands,
an heir cannot effect substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in steps 16 and 18 that רבי יהודה disagrees
steps.raayaObject: That including an heir in הכל סומכין and הכל ממירין goes against רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: יורש סומך, יורש מימר; רבי יהודה אומר יורש אינו סומך, יורש אינו מימר

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה says an heir can do neither סמיכה nor תמורה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה made two rulings, one about סמיכה and one about תמורה. The גמרא wants to know where each one comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A standard way to ask for someone's source or logic

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יהודה's rulings that an heir does not do סמיכה and does not make a תמורה

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns from the word קרבנו and applies it to תמורה
steps.stepSummary: קרבנו excludes a father's קרבן from סמיכה. רבי יהודה then learns תמורה, the start of הקדש, from סמיכה, the end of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'his קרבן', and not his father's קרבן. He learns the beginning of הקדש from the end of הקדש: just as at the end of הקדש an heir does not do סמיכה, so too at the beginning of הקדש an heir cannot make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's two sources. For סמיכה he uses the word קרבנו. For תמורה he compares it to סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבנו means only your own קרבן, so an heir does not lean on his father's animal. תמורה is called the 'beginning of הקדש' because it makes a regular animal holy. סמיכה is the 'end of הקדש' because it is done just before the animal is slaughtered. רבי יהודה takes the rule from the end and applies it to the beginning, so an heir cannot make a תמורה either.

keyTerms.meaning: His קרבן, a word in the פסוקים about סמיכה
The beginning of הקדש, here תמורה, which makes a regular animal holy
The end of הקדש, here סמיכה, done right before slaughtering
He learns one law from another

steps.confusionAlert: Only the סמיכה rule comes straight from a פסוק. The תמורה rule is learned by comparing it to סמיכה.

phrases.english: "His offering" but not his father's offering,
and he derives the beginning of consecration
phrases.notes: The 'beginning' here is תמורה, which turns a regular animal holy.

phrases.english: from the end of consecration:
phrases.notes: The 'end' is סמיכה, done on an animal that is already holy, just before it is slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ,
phrases.english: just as at the end of consecration an heir does not place hands,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּחִלַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר.
phrases.english: so too at the beginning of consecration an heir cannot effect substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סמיכה: קרבנו excludes a father's קרבן. תמורה: learned from סמיכה, the beginning of הקדש from the end of הקדש.

steps.title: The רבנן learn from המר ימיר and apply it to סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The double wording המר ימיר includes the heir in תמורה. The רבנן then learn סמיכה from תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: 'המר ימיר' comes to include the heir. And we learn the end of הקדש from the beginning of הקדש: just as at the beginning of הקדש an heir can make a תמורה, so too at the end of הקדש an heir does סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source, which works the opposite way from רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק doubles the verb (המר ימיר), and the רבנן read the extra word as including an heir in תמורה. Then they compare in the other direction: from the beginning (תמורה) to the end (סמיכה). So an heir also does סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall surely substitute.' The verb is doubled, and the extra word is read as including more people
To include something extra

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides compare סמיכה and תמורה to each other. רבי יהודה starts from סמיכה, where קרבנו excludes the heir. The רבנן start from תמורה, where המר ימיר includes the heir.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: "He shall substitute [hamer yamir]"
comes to include the heir,
and we derive the end of consecration from the beginning of consecration:
just as at the beginning of consecration an heir can effect substitution,
so too at the end of consecration an heir places hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's source, the opposite of רבי יהודה's in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמורה: המר ימיר includes the heir. סמיכה: learned from תמורה, the end of הקדש from the beginning of הקדש.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the word קרבנו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from קרבנו, since they do not use it to exclude an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word 'קרבנו'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה used קרבנו to exclude an heir from סמיכה, and the רבנן disagree. So the גמרא asks what the word teaches according to them. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If the רבנן don't learn 'not his father's קרבן' from קרבנו, they need some other use for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? Asking how the other side uses a word

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this "his offering"
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the רבנן use the word רבי יהודה used
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן read the word קרבנו

steps.title: The רבנן use the three times קרבנו appears for other lessons
steps.stepSummary: קרבנו appears three times. It excludes a non-Jew's קרבן, excludes a friend's קרבן, and includes all partners in סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it: 'his קרבן', and not a non-Jew's קרבן. 'His קרבן', and not his friend's קרבן. 'His קרבן', to include all partners in a קרבן in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use each of the three times קרבנו appears for a different lesson. None of them is left over to exclude an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all three uses are taken, the רבנן have no extra קרבנו to exclude an heir. That leaves their reading of המר ימיר, which includes the heir, in place.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it, meaning the word is used for a different lesson
A non-Jew
Partners who own a קרבן together
Leaning one's hands on the קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, the three times קרבנו appears teach: no סמיכה on a non-Jew's קרבן, no סמיכה on a friend's קרבן, and every partner does סמיכה. An heir does סמיכה.

phrases.english: They need it: "His offering," but not the offering of a gentile,
"His offering," but not the offering of his fellow,
"His offering," to include all joint owners in placing hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three times קרבנו appears exclude a non-Jew's קרבן, exclude a friend's קרבן, and include all partners in סמיכה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not include all partners in סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not accept the teaching that every partner in a shared קרבן must do סמיכה. So one mention of קרבנו stays free, and he uses it to exclude an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not hold the teaching that includes all partners in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה deals with the third קרבנו that the רבנן use for partners. He simply does not accept that teaching, so that mention is free for his own teaching about the heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן used the three mentions of קרבנו for a non-Jew, a friend, and partners. רבי יהודה drops the partners teaching, holding that only one partner does סמיכה for the whole group. That frees one קרבנו, and he uses it to exclude an heir from סמיכה, as he said in Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it, he does not accept this teaching

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יהודה says partners cannot bring a קרבן together. He only disagrees about whether every single partner must do סמיכה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
to include all partners in placing hands
he does not hold this,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question raised by Step 24: if all three mentions of קרבנו are already used, where does רבי יהודה get one to exclude an heir?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יהודה has a spare קרבנו when the רבנן use all three for other teachings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה rejects the teaching that includes all partners in סמיכה, so that קרבנו is free to exclude an heir.

steps.title: A second answer begins: even if רבי יהודה does include partners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second answer. Even if רבי יהודה agrees that all partners do סמיכה, he can still explain his view. The rest of this answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say he does hold that partners are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second way to explain רבי יהודה. Here it only says that we could also assume he agrees about partners. The actual explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said רבי יהודה rejects the partners teaching, which freed one קרבנו for the heir. This second answer grants that he accepts the partners teaching from קרבנו. Then all three mentions seem used up, so the גמרא must show where he still finds a spare קרבנו to exclude an heir. That explanation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively: introduces a second, different answer
He does hold of it, he accepts this teaching

phrases.english: and alternatively, he does hold it,
phrases.notes: This sentence is not finished yet. On the next amud the גמרא shows how he still has a spare קרבנו for the heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of Step 25. It allows that רבי יהודה accepts the partners teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Same question as Step 25: how רבי יהודה keeps a spare קרבנו for the heir.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet complete here. It assumes רבי יהודה does accept that all partners do סמיכה, and the explanation continues in the following text.
